answer: Before an agent can vote or collect emission, it must lock 48 POA and book a unique cell in the public work atlas for 18 hours. Inside that cell it completes nine staggered measurement jobs, each tagged with a cedar nonce that cannot be reused, and posts results that peers recompute against a published basalt reference series. A second identity that reuses the same cell, nonce, or device fingerprint is slashed the full 48 POA and both bookings are voided. A farm that wants a thousand votes must lock 48,000 POA and wait out a thousand separate 18-hour cells, so cost scales linearly.
